subject: Banking
title: Payday Lending Traps
description: A short lesson to help you apply Payday Lending Traps.

hook.text: Payday loans charge 400% annual interest. Borrowers pay $15 per $100 every two weeks.

buildup.text: Payday lenders target low-income neighborhoods. The average borrower makes $30,000 a year and takes 8 loans annually.

discovery.text: 75% of payday loan fees come from borrowers who take 10+ loans per year.

twist.text: Major banks funded payday lenders. Wells Fargo and US Bank invested in companies they'd never lend from directly.

climax.text: Payday lending is legal usury. Banks profit from poverty by funding lenders that charge 400% to the most vulnerable.

punchline.text: 400% interest. 80% repeating. Banks funded the lenders targeting the poor.

quiz.question: What percentage of payday loan fees come from repeat borrowers?

details.summary: Bank partnerships with payday lenders enabled short-term loans with annualized interest rates exceeding 400 percent, trapping vulnerable borrowers in cycles of debt that generated massive profits for both parties.
details.whyItMatters: Payday lending exploits people with no access to affordable credit. Bank involvement gave predatory lending an air of legitimacy while generating billions from the most financially vulnerable populations.
takeaways: Annualized interest rates on payday loans can exceed 400 percent
The average borrower takes out eight loans per year to cover previous ones
Some banks offered their own high-interest payday-style products

faq.question: How do payday loans trap people in debt?
faq.answer: A two-week loan of $300 might cost $45 in fees. If the borrower cannot repay in full, they roll the loan over, paying another $45 fee. Over a year, they may pay $1,000 in fees on a $300 loan.

faq.question: Why do banks partner with payday lenders?
faq.answer: Banks process the loan payments and earn fees from each transaction. Some banks also made deposit advance products that functioned similarly. Regulatory crackdowns have reduced but not eliminated these partnerships.
